Subject: Draft OKR scores and variance callouts

Team — attaching the first pass of final scores and a short variance appendix. Top-level notes:
- Revenue-facing OKRs: some over-performance driven by a one-time channel uplift (callout in appendix tab "Channel uplift").
- Infra & Reliability: missed by 8% against target; primary root-cause traced to delayed infra rollout (see evidence pages 6–8).
- Developer DX: qualitative signals strong, but metric definition drifted mid-quarter; I annotated the evidence where we need to hand back partial credit.

As discussed in the leadership huddle, we need: (1) a one-paragraph narrative per objective for the exec deck, (2) a condensed variance note for the QBR appendix, and (3) a short handback script we can use when communicating with stakeholders.

Attachments: scoring-evidence.pdf, appendix-variance.xlsx

Laura

Adding the appendix with ticket-level counts — see appendix-variance.xlsx. Quick notes:
- Channel uplift: 62% of the revenue delta is attributable to last-mile promo activity (marked tab). We should reflect that as "attribution-adjusted" revenue rather than a pure score bump.
- Reliability: the timeline does show deploy slippage; however, a related config rollback on 10/12 contributed 40% of the impact (evidence in the ticket column).

- "On reliability, the team has scheduled a dedicated postmortem and a hardened rollback plan; we have confidence in the remediation but will reflect the operational gap in the score."

Folks — finalizing and closing the loop on this thread. Below is the consolidated handback we will publish with the QBR appendix; I've drafted the one-paragraph narratives and the brief handback script for customer/stakeholder comms. Please review and, if no objections, I'll publish the appendix to the shared drive and send the external-facing handback to partners next week.

--- Consolidated handback (for QBR appendix) ---
Objective: Revenue & GTM Efficiency
Score: 7/10 (adjusted attribution)
Narrative (80–100 words): Revenue exceeded plan this quarter driven by steady GTM execution and a discrete promotional uplift in week 40. To maintain conservative scoring discipline, the team applied an attribution adjustment that removes the one-time promotional delta from target attainment. The organization is focusing on sustainable expansion levers in the coming quarter and will operationalize the lessons from the promotion playbook.

Objective: System Reliability
Score: 5/10
Narrative (70–90 words): Reliability fell short of expectations due to a delayed infra rollout and a subsequent configuration rollback that amplified impact. The engineering and infra teams have scheduled a targeted postmortem and a revised deploy pipeline to eliminate the class of deployment errors observed. We reflect the operational gap in the score and will track remediation during the next quarter.

Objective: Platform Productivity
Score: 8/10
Narrative (50–70 words): Developer DX initiatives delivered measurable improvements in onboarding time and CI success rates. Metric definition drift required an adjusted interpretation of some signals, which the team has remedied by re-establishing clear measurement windows. The progress is meaningful and will be a plank in next quarter's efficiency push.

Handback script (external-facing):
- "We observed solid GTM progress this quarter; to ensure durable signal, we've adjusted for a one-time promotional uplift and reflected that in our final score."
- "For reliability, we've invested in immediate remediation and will publish postmortem action items in the next 30 days."

If there are no content objections, I will: (1) upload scoring-evidence.pdf and appendix-variance.xlsx to the shared Drive link (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cOKR-QBR-2026) and (2) send the external handback to Acme partners on Monday.

Attachments to publish: scoring-evidence.pdf, appendix-variance.xlsx, qbr-notes.docx

Evelyn Hart
VP, Customer & GTM Initiatives
Redwood Inference
